source.title: Unrecognized node type for community packages with a dot in the npm scope

labels.name: status:in-linear
labels.description: Issue or PR is now in Linear

source.body:
### Bug Description

Community node packages whose npm scope contains a dot (for example `@seven.io/n8n-nodes-seven` or `@explorium.ai/n8n-nodes-explorium`) can be installed and their nodes show up in the node panel, but executing a workflow that uses one of these nodes fails with:

```
Unrecognized node type: @seven.io/n8n-nodes-seven
```

Root cause: the backend derives the package of a full node type with `fullNodeType.split(".")`. For `@seven.io/n8n-nodes-seven.seven` this yields package `@seven` and node `io/n8n-nodes-seven`, so no loader is found. Affected places on current master:

- `packages/cli/src/load-nodes-and-credentials.ts`: `recognizesNode`, `getNode`, `resolveNodeSourcePath`
- `packages/cli/src/modules/type-availability-policies/policy-evaluator.ts`: `nodeTypePackageResolver` (`split(".")[0]`), so a `package` policy rule for such a package never matches its nodes

The same pattern exists in `packages/core`, which the n8n team maintains in-house:

- `packages/core/src/nodes-loader/directory-loader.ts`: `extractNodeTypes`, used for `NODES_INCLUDE` / `NODES_EXCLUDE`
- `packages/core/nodes-testing/load-nodes-and-credentials.ts`: `getNode`

Node names never contain a dot, while npm package names may contain dots in the scope and in the name, so splitting at the last dot fixes all of these.

History: reported before in #15574 (closed by the stale bot), fixed in #25018 (closed as stale) and #41033 (closed because it touched `packages/core`). I will open a PR limited to `packages/cli` and `packages/workflow`; the `packages/core` sites above would need to be handled by the n8n team.

### To Reproduce

1. Start a self-hosted n8n instance.
2. Go to Settings > Community nodes and install `@seven.io/n8n-nodes-seven@0.2.0`.
3. Create a workflow with a Manual Trigger and add the seven node (it is listed in the node panel).
4. Execute the workflow.
5. See the error `Unrecognized node type: @seven.io/n8n-nodes-seven`.

### Expected behavior

Nodes from a community package with a dot in its npm scope execute like nodes from any other community package, and `NODES_INCLUDE` / `NODES_EXCLUDE` as well as `package` rules of type availability policies work for them.

### Debug Info

Not attached from a running instance. The behavior was checked against current master (commit 46761a60, n8n 2.44.0) with unit tests on `LoadNodesAndCredentials.recognizesNode` / `getNode`: `@seven.io/n8n-nodes-seven.seven` is not recognized and `getNode` throws `UnrecognizedNodeTypeError`, while `n8n-nodes-base.httpRequest`, `@n8n/n8n-nodes-langchain.agent` and `n8n-nodes-foo.bar` resolve correctly.

## Environment

### Operating System

macOS 26.6.2

### n8n Version

2.44.0 (master)

### Node.js Version

26.7.0

### Database

SQLite (default)

### Execution mode

main (default)

### Hosting

self hosted

comments.author: cl77
comments.text: Thanks for checking! Right, #34949 / #35221 are about the node-cli name validation. This one is the runtime side: `split('.')` in `load-nodes-and-credentials.ts` (closest older report is #15574, closed by the stale bot). #41042 fixes the cli/workflow part; the remaining `packages/core` sites are listed in the issue description.
